name: Gia Lai
provinceNote: The 2025 merger joined former Bình Định and former Gia Lai into one province still called Gia Lai. The provincial seat is Quy Nhơn on the coast. Travelers use Pleiku for the lake, the volcano, and PXU airport.
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: Morning mist on Biển Hồ is the reason to sleep in Pleiku. The lake, also called Hồ T’Nưng, sits about 7 km north of town, a trace of three extinct volcanoes on the provincial scenic list. Tea slopes share that northern loop, and Chu Đăng Ya, an inactive crater, is about 30 km northeast. Stay in Pleiku when the highland lake is the trip. Quy Nhơn is the coastal capital of the merged province, a different climate and a different night.
getThere: Fly into Pleiku (PXU), about 5 km from the city, or come by road on Quốc lộ 14 and 19
seoTitle: Gia Lai travel guide — Pleiku for the Biển Hồ lake
seoDescription: Sleep in Pleiku for Biển Hồ, the volcanic lake about 7 km north of town, with tea slopes on the same loop and Chu Đăng Ya about 30 km northeast.
intro: You come to Pleiku for the lake. Biển Hồ, also called Hồ T’Nưng, sits about 7 km north, and the Gia Lai provincial portal calls it a trace of three extinct volcanoes. From Phạm Văn Đồng, Quốc lộ 14, turn at the Biển Hồ junction onto Tôn Đức Thắng and walk the shore while the morning mist is still on the water.

Chu Đăng Ya is about 30 km northeast, an inactive crater about 500 m above sea level. Farmers plant the bowl with pumpkin, taro, and corn, and wild sunflowers cover the slopes in the dry-season window. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism names steep, slippery sections on the walk up from Ploi lagri village. Minh Thanh Pagoda stands on the hill above town, built in 1964, with a 72 m gold-painted tower, a po mu wood ceiling, and carved wooden doors. It is not Buu Minh pagoda, the landmark on the road toward the volcano.

Breakfast is two-bowl pho, phở hai tô: dry noodles in one bowl and hot broth in the other, with the fermented black soybean sauce Go Vietnam ties to Gia Lai. Shops concentrate on Nguyen Van Troi through midday. At night, Dien Hong food street, on Nguyen Thien Thuat and Tran Phu in Dien Hong ward, serves the same bowl plus grilled dishes. Vietnam.vn records the street opening on 22 April 2026 with 73 lots, on the old night-market ground. Grilled chicken with cơm lam, sticky rice cooked in bamboo, is the highland lunch or dinner. The Vietnam News Agency names Le Duan alleys as the area in town, and the national tourism walk-up names Tan Son commune after the volcano.

On festival week and on Saturdays, gong ensembles play at Dai Doan Ket Square. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism promotes those Saturday evenings, and Vietnam.vn announces Gong Festival Night in 2026 at 20:00 on 7 November. The series that year runs 30 October through 8 November, with a street festival on 6 November through central Pleiku, Dien Hong, and Hoi Phu. Boat tickets, gate donations, stall prices, and Saturday start times outside that night are Check on arrival.
gettingAround: Pleiku Airport, PXU, is about 5 km from the center. The Gia Lai provincial portal names domestic routes to Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Da Nang. Block times are Check on arrival. Taxis and ride-hail cover the lake, about 7 km north, and Chu Đăng Ya, about 30 km northeast. Ride a motorbike yourself only with the proper license. The provincial introduction names the airport and Quốc lộ 14 and 19, not a train into Pleiku.

Quy Nhơn, the provincial capital since the 2025 merger, is about 180 km by road on the Pleiku portal’s enterprise note. Drive minutes are Check on arrival. Quốc lộ 19 is the coast-to-highlands road. Quốc lộ 14 runs north toward Kon Tum. The walk up Chu Đăng Ya includes steep, slippery sections in wet weather.

stayAreas.name: Near Biển Hồ
stayAreas.summary: Sleep closer to the lake when you want the first light on the water without a cross-town ride.

eat: Two-bowl pho on Nguyen Van Troi in the morning, and again at Dien Hong food street after dark. Grilled chicken with bamboo-tube rice for lunch or dinner. Highland coffee with the slow start of the day. Stall prices are Check on arrival.
interestsBody: Biển Hồ is the morning: a volcanic lake about 7 km north of Pleiku, with the tea dam road on the same loop and Chu Đăng Ya farther northeast.
Minh Thanh Pagoda is the hill stop in town, a 72 m gold-painted tower above the roofs, not Buu Minh on the volcano road.

body: Biển Hồ, also called Hồ T’Nưng, sits about 7 km north of Pleiku. The Gia Lai provincial portal describes it as a trace of three extinct volcanoes. From Phạm Văn Đồng, Quốc lộ 14, turn at the Biển Hồ junction onto Tôn Đức Thắng. Come at first light for mist on the water. Boat hire and tickets are Check on arrival.

The tea slopes are about 12 km north: from Quốc lộ 14, turn on Lê Văn Sỹ for about 3 km, then left along the irrigation dam road. Walk the rows and keep off the harvest paths. Chu Đăng Ya is about 30 km northeast and about 500 m above sea level, planted with pumpkin, taro, and corn. Wild sunflower dates differ by source. Vietnam Tourism names November to December. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism article on Chu Đăng Ya names late October to December. Fees for the lake, the tea slopes, and the volcano are Check on arrival.

season.label: Drier highland months
season.note: Vietnam Tourism calls November to April the drier months, and November to December the wild-sunflower window. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism article on Chu Đăng Ya names late October to December for sunflowers on the volcano. Coffee flowers come around February to April. Heavy rain can slow the highland roads. The 2026 gong festival runs 30 October–8 November; later years are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Pleiku or Quy Nhơn?
faqs.a: Stay in Pleiku for Biển Hồ, Chu Đăng Ya, and PXU airport. Quy Nhơn is the merged province’s coastal capital, about 180 km away on the Pleiku portal’s enterprise note, with its own beach climate. They are not interchangeable nights.

faqs.q: When are the gongs and the sunflowers?
faqs.a: Vietnam Tourism calls November to April the drier months, and November to December the wild-sunflower window. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism article on Chu Đăng Ya names late October to December. The 2026 series is 30 October through 8 November, with Gong Festival Night at 20:00 on 7 November at Dai Doan Ket Square. Later years are Check on arrival. Saturday gong evenings are also promoted, and start times outside that festival night are Check on arrival.

Two-bowl pho, dry noodles in one bowl and broth in the other, along Nguyen Van Troi through midday. Go Vietnam ties the fermented black soybean sauce to Gia Lai. Dien Hong food street serves the same bowl at night. Stall prices are Check on arrival.
